sections.h2: How can I sell my house fast in Yakima, WA?
sections.html:
A sale to a cash buyer is typically the quickest path, since it removes the buyer's mortgage approval and appraisal from the schedule. A listing can still bring a higher price if the house shows well and you can wait for the right offer.

Yakima is the seat of Yakima County and the 11th most populous city in Washington, in the Upper Valley of Yakima County, about 60 miles southeast of Mount Rainier. The Census Bureau estimates 97,458 residents as of July 1, 2025. West Valley and Terrace Heights are unincorporated suburbs that are treated as part of greater Yakima, so confirm whether your address is inside city limits before you check any city rule.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show about Yakima housing?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's QuickFacts table reports the following for Yakima city.

At $297,600, Yakima's median home value is well below Wenatchee's $433,700 and Vancouver's $462,400. About 46 percent of housing units are not owner-occupied, so rentals make up a large part of the local market.

sections.h2: What drives the Yakima housing market?
sections.html:
Agriculture does. The Yakima Valley produces apples, peaches, pears, cherries and melons, along with peppers, corn and beans, and as of 2011 it grew 77 percent of the hops harvested in the United States. Many residents came to the valley to pick, process, market and support that farm economy.

The city's 2022 financial report, summarized on Wikipedia, lists the largest employers:

  • Yakima Valley Memorial Hospital, 2,500 employees
  • Walmart (Yakima, Sunnyside and Grandview), 1,700
  • Yakima School District, 1,594
  • Zirkle Fruit and Washington Fruit and Produce, 1,500 each
  • Yakama Nation Government Operations, 1,289

Downtown Yakima was long the retail hub, but the regional retail core has moved to Union Gap, where a renovated mall and new stores opened.

sections.h2: How does Yakima's climate affect a house?
sections.html:
Yakima has a cold semi-arid climate, with a location in a rain shadow that holds precipitation to about 8 inches a year. Annual snowfall averages 21.6 inches, mostly in December and January, and the average last freeze of spring comes on May 13, with the first freeze of fall around September 30.

Summers are hot. The city averages 40.2 afternoons a year at 90 degrees or higher and 5.7 at 100 degrees or higher, and it reached 113 degrees on June 29, 2021. Day-to-night swings in July average nearly 35 degrees. Roofing, attic insulation, cooling equipment and exterior paint carry the load from those swings, so any receipts or warranties for them are worth collecting before you list. Yakima sits at 1,095 feet above sea level.

sections.h2: Which schools and highways matter to Yakima buyers?
sections.html:
The Yakima School District runs four high schools in the city: Davis High School, Eisenhower High School, Stanton Academy and Yakima Online High School. West Valley High School is in the West Valley School District, and East Valley High School, just east of Terrace Heights, is in the East Valley School District.

Interstate 82 is the main freeway, linking Yakima to Ellensburg and the Tri-Cities with onward routes to Seattle and Oregon. U.S. Route 12 crosses the north of the city and joins I-82 and U.S. Route 97 on the east side. State Route 24 ends in Yakima and leads to Moxee and the farm areas to the east, while State Route 821 follows the Yakima River canyon toward Ellensburg. The average commute for city workers is 17.8 minutes.

sections.h2: Which repairs need a permit in Yakima?
sections.html:
The city's Code Administration office explains this on its permit process page. Some jobs can be applied for online without plan review:

  • Same-for-same plumbing and mechanical change-outs
  • Residential reroofs that are tear off and reroof only
  • Water and sewer line replacements
  • Residential re-siding
  • Oil tank abandonment and removal
  • Woodstove or wood-burning device installation

A remodel needs a building permit application plus plans showing existing and proposed floor plans and wall details. Land use review may be needed first, and the building permit is not issued until it is approved. Electrical permits go through the state Department of Labor and Industries, at (509) 454-3700 for the Yakima office. Questions about the process go to codes@yakimawa.gov or (509) 575-6126, and applications run through buildingyakima.com.

sections.h2: What if my Yakima house is vacant or in poor shape?
sections.html:
The city responds to complaints about conditions on private property, including garbage, overgrown yards, junk vehicles and vacant buildings that are open to unauthorized entry. In March 2024 the City Council adopted the 2021 International Property Maintenance Code, with local changes, as YMC Chapter 11.40.

The Code Compliance page says anyone directly affected by a notice or order can appeal to the hearing examiner, provided a written appeal is filed within 20 days after service. Reports and questions go through the Yak Back portal or the hotline at (509) 576-6657. If you inherited a vacant house and have not yet secured it, securing it early gives you more options with a buyer, whether that buyer is a family or an investor planning a rehab.

sections.h2: How does a deed transfer work in Yakima County?
sections.html:
Yakima County splits the job between two offices. According to the county's property transfer page, every transfer of real property needs a Real Estate Excise Tax Affidavit processed through the County Treasurer's Office with the conveyance document. The Auditor's Recording Division then records the document. Excise tax and transfer fees must be paid in cash or certified funds.

The same order applies statewide under RCW 82.45.090, which keeps the auditor from recording a deed ahead of the tax payment or a not-due notation. Ask the Yakima County Treasurer for the amount that applies at your price, since it includes both a state and a local portion.

A mobile home follows a different path. If the sale does not require moving it, a Mobile Home Real Estate Excise Tax Affidavit is used, and the Auditor's Vehicle Licensing Division handles the new owner's title. Property taxes must be paid in full before that processing. For a house, the seller also fills out the condition form from RCW 64.06.020 and gives it to the buyer shortly after contract, five business days being the default limit.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Yakima house with an old roof or siding?
faqs.a: Yes. Plenty of buyers take older roofs and siding as they are. If you decide to fix the roof or siding first, the city lets residential reroofs (tear off and reroof only) and re-siding be applied for online without plan review.

faqs.q: What payment form does Yakima County accept for excise tax?
faqs.a: Cash or certified funds. The county's property transfer page states that excise tax and transfer fees must be paid in cash or certified funds.

faqs.q: Can I appeal a city notice about my Yakima property?
faqs.a: Yes. Anyone directly affected by a property maintenance decision, notice or order may appeal to the hearing examiner. The written appeal must be filed within 20 days after the notice is served.

faqs.q: Where do I get an electrical permit in Yakima?
faqs.a: Electrical permits and inspections come from the state Department of Labor and Industries, not the city. The Yakima office is at 15 W Yakima Ave., Suite 100, and the phone number is (509) 454-3700.

faqs.q: Is my house in the Yakima School District?
faqs.a: It depends on the address. The Yakima School District runs Davis, Eisenhower, Stanton Academy and Yakima Online, while West Valley and East Valley are separate districts. Confirm with the district before you describe the schools to a buyer.
